findings.title: Do not pipe an unpinned remote script into a root shell
findings.whyItBreaks: The build downloads https://example.com/install.sh and immediately executes it with sh as root, with no pinned version, checksum, or signature verification. Anyone who compromises or changes that URL, its redirects, or its hosting gains arbitrary code execution in the build context and can poison the resulting image, steal build secrets mounted or present during build, or alter /app before it is copied. The image content also becomes non-reproducible because the same Dockerfile can produce different images without any repository change. In addition, curl is invoked without --fail and its output is piped to sh, so some download failures are masked by the pipeline exit status being taken from sh.

findings.title: Stop discarding ErrMissing in exported LoadOrDefault
findings.whyItBreaks: Load returns "", ErrMissing for a missing key at src/store.go:10 but "", nil for a present empty value at src/store.go:12. LoadOrDefault discards the error with `v, _ := Load(key, m)` at src/store.go:16 and returns "" for both cases, so public callers cannot distinguish failure from a legitimate empty value and may persist or report the fallback as real data. No in-repo caller is required for this to be a defect because the exported signature itself forces that conflation.

findings.title: Wait for goroutines before Run returns
findings.whyItBreaks: Previously Run returned only after every send on results completed, so a caller could safely close(results) or stop receiving after Run returned. Now Run returns immediately while detached goroutines still execute results <- j*2 at line 8: closing the channel after Run races with those sends and can panic with 'send on closed channel', and if the receiver stops or ctx is cancelled the goroutines block forever because neither the send nor ctx.Done() is selected on (ctx at line 5 is unused). It also spawns one goroutine per job with no bound or completion signal.

findings.title: Preserve input ordering of results
findings.whyItBreaks: The original loop sent j*2 in jobs order, so a receiver reading len(jobs) values got results in the same order as the input — the de facto contract of this exported function. The goroutine-per-job version delivers values in scheduler order, so positional consumers silently associate results with the wrong jobs.

findings.title: Honor the new Log tag argument instead of discarding it
findings.whyItBreaks: Log is exported and now accepts tag ...string, which by its signature promises callers can tag log output, but the body at src/logger.go:4 only executes println(message) and never reads tag. A caller adopting the new API, e.g. Log("failed", "auth"), gets untagged output silently, so tag-based filtering/grouping loses data with no error.

findings.title: Restore AND in canDeleteRecord to prevent unauthorized deletion
findings.whyItBreaks: Previously deletion required both isAdmin and matching tenantId. With OR, any non-admin session whose tenantId matches can delete any record in that tenant (ownerId is never checked), and any admin can delete records in any other tenant, enabling privilege escalation, cross-tenant data loss, and tenant-isolation bypass through this exported authorization predicate.

findings.title: Stop swallowing parse errors as DEFAULTS and persisting them
findings.whyItBreaks: Previously parseSettings threw on JSON.parse failure, non-string theme, or non-number fontSize, so updateFontSize aborted before save. Now the catch-all returns {...DEFAULTS}, indistinguishable from a legitimate {theme:"light",fontSize:14}; updateFontSize at src/settings.ts:20-22 then unconditionally sets fontSize and calls save(JSON.stringify(settings)), overwriting corrupt/invalid stored settings with defaults and masking the corruption instead of surfacing it.

findings.title: Restore artifacts to the same commit as builtFrom
findings.whyItBreaks: builtFrom is build.ref(branch) at line 12, but artifacts are fetched via artifactsAt(build.ref("verified")) at lines 13-14. Whenever the branch ref and the "verified" ref resolve to different commits, the returned BuildReport pairs builtFrom=<branch commit> with artifacts belonging to the verified commit, so consumers receive and may publish/report artifacts that were not built from builtFrom. Before this change both fields used the same commit.

findings.title: Restore `limit` cap in recentEntries for positive limits
findings.whyItBreaks: Documented contract at src/feed.ts:1 promises 'at most `limit` entries', but the new body returns the full reversed array whenever limit>0 (e.g. recentEntries(100 entries, 20) returns 100, not 20). Relying caller renderFeed at src/feed.ts:9-11 allocates `new Array<string>(20)` assuming page.length<=20; with >20 inputs the loop writes past index 19, auto-extending the array and returning more than 20 entries.

findings.title: Fix entry-count to count only emitted live rows
findings.whyItBreaks: Rows are now built only from live entries, but headerLines still receives entries.length. With one live and one stale entry, the output contains one row while declaring '# entry-count: 2', making the exported manifest internally inconsistent for any consumer that validates or uses the count.

findings.title: Restore removed shippingQuote export from orders module
findings.whyItBreaks: Previously `shippingQuote` was exported from src/orders.ts; the head only imports quoteShipping internally and exports Order and orderTotal. Any existing consumer doing `import { shippingQuote } from "./orders"` (or the package equivalent) now fails with TS2305 / missing export, even though equivalent logic moved to src/pricing/shipping.ts as quoteShipping. No in-repo caller masks this because orderTotal was updated internally.

findings.title: Restore execute() instead of unconditionally throwing
findings.whyItBreaks: The exported execute(input: string): string previously returned input.toUpperCase(), but now throws Error("always fails") for every input. Any caller receives an exception instead of the promised string, making the repo's only exported function unusable.

findings.title: Remove viewer rejection from isEligible to preserve read-only handling
findings.whyItBreaks: Substituting {status:'active',role:'viewer',attempts:0}: previously isEligible returned true and handle returned 'read-only' at line 25. Now isEligible returns false at line 18, so handle returns 'rejected' at line 24 and the viewer read-only branch at line 25 is unreachable. The eligibility gate therefore rejects a distinct action that was legitimately approvable on its own.

findings.title: Stop payment gate from blocking draft saves
findings.whyItBreaks: canProceed now requires payment==="paid". Substituting {state:"draft",payment:"missing"}: previously canProceed=true, now false, so saveDraft at src/actions.ts:9 returns "blocked" instead of "saved". Saving a draft is legitimately approvable before payment; the payment condition legitimately governs submitOrder at src/actions.ts:4, not saveDraft.

findings.title: Restore snapshot files to requested channel's head commit
findings.whyItBreaks: publishSnapshot sets Snapshot.commit to repo.headCommit(channel) but Snapshot.files to repo.filesAt(repo.headCommit("stable")). Whenever channel's head differs from stable's head, the snapshot publishes stable's files while claiming they belong to channel's commit, so consumers receive mismatched commit/files content.

findings.title: Use the new `limit` parameter instead of the hardcoded count
findings.whyItBreaks: The public signature `build(prefix, limit=10)` promises capping by `limit`, but the body sets `max_count = 10` and loops over `range(max_count)` without reading `limit`. Substituting `limit=5`, `limit=0`, or `limit=20` still returns exactly 10 items, so any caller passing a non-default limit receives the wrong-sized result.

findings.title: Enforce positive validation in parse_positive_int
findings.whyItBreaks: The renamed public function parse_positive_int promises that it returns a positive integer, but its body is only return int(value). Therefore parse_positive_int('-5') returns -5 instead of rejecting it, and the in-repo caller charge at src/validators.py:6-7 propagates that as a -500 result.

findings.title: Restore copy so apply_values does not mutate caller's DataFrame
findings.whyItBreaks: Previously apply_values operated on df.copy() and returned a new DataFrame, leaving the caller's df unchanged. Now df.loc[df["key"] == key, "value"] = value mutates the input in place and returns the same object, so any caller reusing, retrying with, or comparing against its original DataFrame silently sees the overwritten values (aliasing/data-corruption).

findings.title: Rename to parse_positive_int promises positivity body never enforces
findings.whyItBreaks: The new public name promises a positive integer, but s.parse::<i64>().unwrap_or(0) returns -5 for "-5" and 0 for "0" or unparsable input. The only in-repo caller, charge at src/parse.rs:6, relies on the result arithmetically as n * 100 with no positivity validation, so charge("-5") produces -500 instead of a rejected or non-negative amount. Because the function is pub, external callers are likewise entitled to trust the positive contract.

findings.title: Fix dbg! move of items that breaks compilation
findings.whyItBreaks: dbg!(items) takes ownership of Vec<String> (not Copy) and its returned value is dropped as a statement temporary, so items.len() on line 3 is use of a moved value (E0382) and the crate does not compile. If borrowed instead it would still emit uncontrolled stderr debug output of caller data in production.
